subject: biology
title: ATP
key_idea: ATP is the molecule cells use to pass energy to reactions. Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and Pi releases a small, usable amount of energy at once. Respiration and photosynthesis use energy to join ADP and Pi back into ATP.

blocks.text: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is a phosphorylated nucleotide. It is made of three parts joined together.

items: Ribose, a pentose (five-carbon) sugar.
Adenine, a nitrogenous base.
Three phosphate groups in a chain, joined to the ribose.
ADP (adenosine diphosphate) has the same structure but only two phosphate groups.

items.meaning: A pentose sugar joined to a nitrogenous base and one or more phosphate groups.
An inorganic phosphate group, a free phosphate ion.
Adding a phosphate group to a molecule.

items: ATP = ribose + adenine + three phosphate groups.
ADP has two phosphate groups, ATP has three.
ATP is a nucleotide derivative, closely related to the nucleotides in RNA.

blocks.text: ATP is broken down by hydrolysis when a cell needs energy. It is rebuilt by condensation when energy is available.

items: The enzyme ATP hydrolase catalyses the hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and Pi.
The reaction releases energy, which can be coupled to an energy-requiring reaction in the cell.
The released Pi can phosphorylate other compounds. This often makes them more reactive.
ADP and Pi are joined by a condensation reaction.
The enzyme ATP synthase catalyses it, during respiration and during photosynthesis.
This phosphorylation of ADP needs energy, which comes from the oxidation of respiratory substrates or from light.

blocks.label: ATP and ADP
where: Forward reaction: hydrolysis, catalysed by ATP hydrolase
Reverse reaction: condensation, catalysed by ATP synthase

items: ATP hydrolase breaks ATP down to ADP and Pi, releasing energy.
ATP synthase joins ADP and Pi, using energy.
Pi from ATP can phosphorylate a compound and make it more reactive.

sections.heading: Why ATP is the universal energy currency

blocks.text: Every living cell uses ATP, which is why it is called the universal energy currency. Its features suit this job.

items: Hydrolysis releases a small amount of energy, so little is wasted as heat and the energy can be matched to one reaction.
It releases energy in a single step, so the supply is immediate.
It is soluble and can move around the cell to where it is needed.
It cannot leave the cell, so each cell keeps its own supply.
It is made in respiration and in photosynthesis, then used in many different reactions.

blocks.text: ATP cannot be stored in large amounts. Cells turn it over constantly, so it is resynthesised as fast as it is used.
Cells use ATP from respiration for active transport, movement such as muscle contraction, and anabolic reactions such as making proteins and DNA.

items: ATP releases a small, manageable amount of energy in one step.
It is made in all cells, and used by all cells.
It is a short-term energy carrier, not a long-term store.

checks.q: Name the three parts of an ATP molecule.
checks.a: Ribose (a pentose sugar), adenine (a nitrogenous base) and three phosphate groups.

checks.q: Describe how the hydrolysis of ATP can supply energy to a cell, and name the enzyme that catalyses it.
checks.a: ATP is hydrolysed to ADP and Pi, catalysed by ATP hydrolase. This releases energy, which is coupled to an energy-requiring reaction. The Pi can also phosphorylate another compound, making it more reactive.

checks.q: Give two features of ATP that make it suitable as the universal energy currency.
checks.a: Any two from: it releases a small amount of energy at a time, so little is wasted; it releases energy in one step, so supply is immediate; it is soluble and moves around the cell; it is made in all cells by respiration or photosynthesis and used by many reactions.
